standards.name: Audiovisual Core (TDWG)
standards.abstract: Audiovisual Core (AC) is a vocabulary-based metadata standard for describing biodiversity-related multimedia resources and collections (still images, sound, video, 3D models, animations, etc.). It is maintained by the Audiovisual Core Maintenance Group under Biodiversity Information Standards (TDWG / GBIF collaborations). The standard provides a term list (record-level and access-level terms), controlled vocabularies (e.g. content description, format, subjectPart, subjectOrientation, subtype, variant), and guidance on serializing records so users and aggregators can determine whether media are fit for particular biodiversity science uses before acquiring the media.

classification.rationale: The source material is a machine-oriented vocabulary and term list: it documents named metadata terms (with URIs, labels, definitions, repeatability and usage notes) and multiple controlled-vocabulary lists. The documents present concrete field-level structure (term entries and controlled value lists), not just prose guidance, so this is a TABLE-style metadata vocabulary.

ac:identifier.name: Identifier
ac:identifier.descr: A globally unique identifier for the Audiovisual Core record / resource (GUID).
ac:identifier.evidence: One of these, the value of Identifier is a Globally Unique IDentifier (GUID), which may have been assigned to the resource by an external authority or by the provider of the metadata record.

ac:type.name: Type
ac:type.descr: The resource type (e.g. values from Dublin Core Type vocabulary) indicating the kind of multimedia resource.
ac:type.evidence: A Multimedia Resource is anything that a provider identifies as belonging to one of the possible values of the AC Type term and optionally one or more of the Subtype term values.

ac:metadataLanguage.name: metadataLanguage
ac:metadataLanguage.evidence: This document ... contains at least the four mandatory terms, which provide an identifier, a resource type, the language of the description, and copyright information.

ac:rights.name: copyright / rights information
ac:rights.descr: Copyright or rights information associated with the resource / record.
ac:rights.evidence: This document ... contains at least the four mandatory terms, which provide an identifier, a resource type, the language of the description, and copyright information.

ac:hasServiceAccessPoint.name: hasServiceAccessPoint
ac:hasServiceAccessPoint.descr: A service access point describes a retrievable digital representation of the resource (e.g. a URL plus access-level metadata such as format, size, variant). A record may have multiple serviceAccessPoint entries.
ac:hasServiceAccessPoint.type: object (ServiceAccessPoint: url(string), format(ontology_term), extent/size(string or integer), variant(controlled_vocabulary), license(string))
ac:hasServiceAccessPoint.evidence: One such term, serviceAccessPoint plays a special role in helping to retrieve the resource that the record describes. A multimedia resource may have more than one serviceAccessPoint, each of which is described by values of one or more access-level terms.

ac:CVtermLiteral.name: ac:CVtermLiteral (content description literal)
ac:CVtermLiteral.descr: Literal-valued controlled vocabulary for describing content of (all or part of) a media item. Intended to be used together with Iptc4xmpExt:CVterm (IRI-valued).
ac:CVtermLiteral.type: controlled_vocabulary (string values drawn from ACCD content description vocabulary)
ac:CVtermLiteral.evidence: This document includes terms intended to be used as controlled values for Audiovisual Core terms Iptc4xmpExt:CVterm and ac:CVtermLiteral.

dcterms:format / dc:format.name: dc:format / dcterms:format
dcterms:format / dc:format.descr: Physical or electronic format of a media item (recommended values: Internet Media Types / MIME types, physical media strings, or common file extensions).
dcterms:format / dc:format.evidence: This document includes terms intended to be used as a controlled value for Dublin Core terms dc:format and dcterms:format ... The entry for the property dc:format in the Audiovisual Core term list document specifies that three kinds of string values are RECOMMENDED: Internet Media Types (MIME types), special string values for physical media, or commonly used file extensions.

ac:subjectOrientation.name: subjectOrientation / ac:subjectOrientationLiteral
ac:subjectOrientation.descr: Viewing orientation relative to an organism or part of an organism depicted in a media item or region of interest.
ac:subjectOrientation.evidence: The Audiovisual Core term subjectOrientation describes the viewing orientation relative to an organism or part of an organism depicted in a media item or region of interest. The subjectOrientation Controlled Vocabulary provides terms that should be used as values for ac:subjectOrientation and its literal-valued analog ac:subjectOrientationLiteral.

ac:subjectPart.name: subjectPart / ac:subjectPartLiteral
ac:subjectPart.descr: Part of an organism (morphology, behaviour, environment) depicted in a media item or region of interest.
ac:subjectPart.evidence: The Audiovisual Core term subjectPart describes the part of an organism morphology, behaviour, environment depicted in a media item or region of interest. The subjectPart Controlled Vocabulary provides terms that should be used as values for ac:subjectPart and its literal-valued analog ac:subjectPartLiteral.

ac:variant.name: variant / ac:variantLiteral
ac:variant.descr: Describes size, extent, and availability of the Service Access Point for a media item (examples: Thumbnail, Trailer, quality variants).
ac:variant.evidence: Audiovisual Core uses the terms ac:variant and ac:variantLiteral to provide information about the size, extent, and availability of the Service Access Point of a media item. This controlled vocabulary provides values for those terms.

ac:subtype.name: subtype / ac:subtypeLiteral
ac:subtype.descr: Refines the media type to a more specific class (e.g. Photograph, Drawing, Film, Animation, Diagram).
ac:subtype.type: controlled_vocabulary (class terms / SKOS or RDFS classes)
ac:subtype.evidence: Audiovisual Core uses the terms ac:subtype and ac:subtypeLiteral to refine the type of a media item to a level more specific than the Dublin Core Type Vocabulary, http://purl.org/dc/dcmitype/. This controlled vocabulary provides values for ac:subtype and ac:subtypeLiteral.

ac:resourceCreationTechnique.name: resourceCreationTechnique
ac:resourceCreationTechnique.descr: Information about how the resource was created (capture modality, processing steps, software, specimen preparation etc.).
ac:resourceCreationTechnique.evidence: scan compilation software	any software used to create the final media file from 'raw scan data' whatever that may be	ac:resourceCreationTechnique

ac:derivedFrom.name: derivedFrom / related resource reference
ac:derivedFrom.descr: Reference to a parent or related media resource (identifier, DOI, accession).
ac:derivedFrom.evidence: parent media file MorphoSource number	the MorphoSource media number pertaining to the dataset used to create a media file	ac:derivedFrom

standards.notes: I extracted the principal vocabulary fields and controlled vocabularies documented in the Audiovisual Core normative and controlled-vocabulary documents. Each table field above is supported by a verbatim quote from the source materials (see 'evidence'). The AC standard contains many more term and controlled-value entries (the List of Terms and the controlled vocabularies are extensive). If you want, I can expand this export to include every individual AC term URI and every controlled-value IRI as separate table rows.
